newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek navy aid ship waits off rebel-held Sarande.
newsitem.headline: Greek navy aid ship waits off rebel-held Sarande.

text.p: The Greek navy minesweeper Atalante waited off the coast of the Albanian rebel-held port of Sarande on Thursday with a cargo of food and medicine, a defence ministry spokesman said.
The captain was waiting until the rebel council in the town, seized 10 days ago, organised a committee to receive and distribute the humanitarian aid.
The spokesman said Greece was concerned that the arrival of the ship in the town, where widespread looting has taken place, would be an invitation for trouble.

As soon as the committee was formed to receive the aid, the Atalante would dock, he said. A private freighter was taking on donations in the Greek port of Piraeus near Athens and planned to set out for Sarande on Thursday or Friday.
Sarande, just across from the Greek island of Corfu and near the northern border, has been at the mercy of armed gangs which stole weapons from state arsenals last week.
The gangs and local residents have looted and robbed over the past 10 days.
